recipes.name: Allie's Delicious Baked Dumplings
ingredients_raw: 1 (17.5 ounce) package frozen puff pastry, thawed
4 Granny Smith apples - peeled, cored and halved

steps.text: Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Lightly grease a baking sheet.
Roll out each sheet of pastry to measure 12x12 inches. Cut into quarters, to make 8 - 6 inch squares.

In a small bowl, combine sugar, bread crumbs, cinnamon and nutmeg. Brush a pastry square with beaten egg. Place 1 tablespoon bread crumb mixture in center. Place one apple half, core side down, over bread crumbs. Top with another tablespoon of mixture. Pull up four corners of pastry and pinch sides together to seal seams completely. Repeat with remaining apples.

Brush each dumpling with beaten egg. Place in preheated oven for 15 minutes, then reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and continue baking 25 minutes more, until lightly browned. Let cool completely at room temperature.
To make icing, combine confectioners' sugar and vanilla and enough milk to make a drizzling consistency. Drizzle over cooled dumplings. Serve the same day.

raw_recipe.headline: Allie's Delicious Baked Dumplings
raw_recipe.description: Tart apples are seasoned with cinnamon, sugar and nutmeg, then baked in puff pastry and drizzled with icing.

review.reviewBody: I've made this recipe for guests and family and have always had rave reviews. I've learned to look for smaller apples as I find it difficult to strech the quartered puff pastry dough over the larger ones. It is now a staple dessert in my family. Really great!! Pat

These were easy and good! I could tell immediately 3 tblspns cinnamon is way too much. I halved the sugar, using combination of white and brown sugar, added two teaspoons cinnamon and 1/2 tspn nutmeg, and less than 1/4 cup
bread crumbs. I followed suggestion to
chop the apples (2 was enough), and the biggest thing was working the pastry dough to make sure I sealed the edges. I'm sure I'll improve. Anyway, some liquid did run out, but they were 
excellent. Will make often, thanks Nyred!

Super delicious! I made these this morning as a New Years Day breakfast treat. I used Macintosh apples instead (only because I forgot which kind was specified while I was at the store) so I cut the sugar in half. I also skipped the drizzle so it wouldn't be too sweet for breakfast but I think I'll add it anyway next time.

This is an amazing recipe... Fantastic! I made four individual dumplings - and one big one... basted all with egg wash, and then saved them in the refrigerator until I was ready to cook them. Gorgeous and Delicious!

I made these last night and they turned out pretty good. The only problem I had was that all but one popped open (my daughter says they blossomed) almost immediately in the oven and so the corners got a little burnt and crispy. 

I didn't put as much of the cinnamon/sugar mixture as the recipe called for because it just seemed a little excessive and I believe a tiny dollop of butter under each apple would have carmelized the sugar better for a more uniform taste throughout.

Delicious recipe. I made the recipe as written the first time. After that, I made just a few changes. Instead of 1c. white sugar, I used 1/2 cup of an equal mix brown/white sugar. I also decreased the amount of cinnamon (to taste) and chopped the apples into coarse chunks. I've also used this recipe with fresh and canned peaches. I think you could use any type of fruit filling for a quick and easy personal sized pie. This is a definite keeper!

Nice recipe. I made half of the recipe because I didn't need 8 servings at the time but between my boyfriend and I we ate all 4 servings! As suggested by previous reviewers I chopped the apples into chunks, didn't use the bread crumbs but followed the rest of the recipe to the letter. My puff pastry got too brown even after reducing the temp. as directed. Maybe the starting temp. should be 400. Anyone have an opinion on that?
I made it ahead and baked it off later. Delicious!!

This was good but next time I will cut the apple in pieces and bake for a shorter amount of time. Everything was done but it was hard to eat. Also, I sprinkle the tops with raw sugar before I baked them.

This was good but next time I will cut the apple in pieces and bake for a shorter amount of time. Everything was done but it was hard to eat. Also, I sprinkle the tops with raw sugar before I baked them.

this is a great recipe, it came out perfect the first time and everyone loved them, I added some dried cranberries and made the filling with a little more butter and spice, it was so good...I will be making this one again
So easy and delicious! Cut down a bit on the sugar because I used sweeter apples. I will make this again for sure!
Easy & delicious!
The apple dumplings are easy to make and taste great. I'd love to have a similar recipe with phyllo pastry which has no fat for people with cholesterol problems...like myself!

Made this for guest and they LOVED it. Very easy and GREAT taste. Will make this again.
Awesome! Had no problems with this! My husband said it was restaurant quality! Thank you!
These were really good! I cut the apple halves in half and served them with vanilla bean ice cream. My daughter and boyfriend gave them thumbs up as well.
